The Lecture 12 presentation defines the examinable scope. Meyer Chapter 9 is used to reinforce mechanisms, terminology, and clinical or experimental examples that support that lecture scope.

## Lecture concepts

### 1. Most humans are regular users

of psychoactive drugs. Caffeine.

**What to know:**
- of psychoactive drugs
- Caffeine
- Alcohol
- Nicotine
- Cannabis

**Meyer connection:** Review the chapter discussion of **substance use, misuse and addiction** and use it to explain the mechanism behind the lecture point rather than memorizing the slide wording alone.

### 2. Most humans use psychoactive drugs without experiencing addiction

~4% experienced drug addiction in the past year. ~10% experienced drug addiction in their lives.

**What to know:**
- ~4% experienced drug addiction in the past year
- ~10% experienced drug addiction in their lives
- If >50% of individuals try illicit drugs, then >80% do not struggle with addiction
- i.e. Drug use is not pathological but rather a normal part of the human experience
- Despite low rates, addiction has a tremendous negative effect on individuals and society Addiction 3 Coca leaf tea

**Meyer connection:** Review the chapter discussion of **reward and reinforcement** and use it to explain the mechanism behind the lecture point rather than memorizing the slide wording alone.

### 3. Addiction is a nuanced term surrounded by stigma

Addiction vs. dependence vs. substance abuse vs. substance use disorder vs. person who uses drugs?. Self stigma, social stigma, structural stigma.

**What to know:**
- Addiction vs. dependence vs. substance abuse vs. substance use disorder vs. person who uses drugs?
- Self stigma, social stigma, structural stigma
- Majority of people who struggle with addiction don’t receive any support (~75%)
- Common false refrain: “addiction is a failure of willpower”
- Small ways to help: person-first language*, understand the neurobiological basis of addiction, get a naloxone kit, take an evidence-based approach *for addiction specifically Addiction 4

**Meyer connection:** Review the chapter discussion of **tolerance, dependence and withdrawal** and use it to explain the mechanism behind the lecture point rather than memorizing the slide wording alone.

### 4. William S. Burroughs, Junky

one morning and decide to be a drug addict. It takes at least three months’ shooting twice a day to get any habit at all. … The questions, of course, could be asked: Why did you ever try narcotics? Why did you continue using it long enough to become an addict? You become a narcotics addict because you do not have strong motivations in the other direction. Junk wins by default. I tried it as a matter of curiosity. I drifted along taking shots when I could score. I ended up hooked. Most addicts I have talked to report a similar experience. They did not start using drugs for any reason they can remember. They just drifted along until they got hooked. If you have never been addicted, you can have no clear idea what it means to need junk with the addict’s special need. You don’t decide to be an addict. One morning you wake up sick and you’re an addict. (Junky, Prologue, p. xxxviii) 5.

**What to know:**
- one morning and decide to be a drug addict. It takes at least three months’ shooting twice a day to get any habit at all. … The questions, of course, could be asked: Why did you ever try narcotics? Why did you continue using it long enough to become an addict? You become a narcotics addict because you do not have strong motivations in the other direction. Junk wins by default. I tried it as a matter of curiosity. I drifted along taking shots when I could score. I ended up hooked. Most addicts I have talked to report a similar experience. They did not start using drugs for any reason they can remember. They just drifted along until they got hooked. If you have never been addicted, you can have no clear idea what it means to need junk with the addict’s special need. You don’t decide to be an addict. One morning you wake up sick and you’re an addict. (Junky, Prologue, p. xxxviii) 5
